title: Chevy C/K Pickup Engines by Year (1960–1998)
description: Every factory engine in the Chevrolet C10, K10, C1500 and K1500 half-ton pickup by year, 1960–1998: sixes, small and big blocks, diesels and the 454 SS.
intro: Chevrolet's C/K trucks ran from 1960 to 1998; C means two-wheel drive and K four-wheel drive. This page covers the half-ton models: the C10 and K10 through 1987 and the C1500 and K1500 from 1988. The Silverado name, a trim level until then, became its own model for 1999.
Pick a year to see every engine offered that model year, with its code, rated horsepower and the trims it came in. Each engine links to its full specs.
The first C/K trucks used Chevrolet's 235 and 230 sixes, the 261 and 292 sixes and the 283 V8, with the 327 added for 1966.

The 1967 redesign kept the 250 and 292 sixes and offered small-block V8s up to the 350. The C10 could be ordered with a big block from 1968: the 396, then the 402, which Chevrolet badged as a 400. Ratings are SAE net from 1972.

The square-body trucks ran from the 250 six to the 454 V8, which was offered in the half-ton through 1979. GM's 6.2 diesel arrived for 1982 and the 4.3 V6 for 1985. For 1987 the half-tons were renamed R10 and V10 when the new C/K trucks were announced.

generations.name: GMT400
intro: The GMT400 C/K 1500 used the 4.3 V6, the 5.0 and 5.7 V8s and diesels, plus the 454 SS of 1990–1993. Vortec heads arrived for 1996.
